expected.body:
Los Angeles Panther raids and detention

Contemporary reporting places Gilbert Parker, also called Gil, in New County Jail after the raid on Central Avenue headquarters. The Party reported that he had been beaten following his arrest.

The December 8, 1969 Los Angeles police raids targeted Black Panther premises at Central Avenue, the Toure Community Center and a residence on 55th Street. The Party denounced the operation as political repression. Contemporary Party reports are attributed as such; their allegations of mistreatment are not presented as independent court findings.

Individual verdicts, physical release dates and time actually detained are recorded only where supported. The broader trial included acquittals on serious counts and some weapons-conspiracy convictions. It would be inaccurate to describe every raid defendant as acquitted of every charge.

Sources

  • The Black Panther, December 20, 1969, printed pages 2, 10–11 and 13: named custody reports
  • The Black Panther, December 27, 1969, printed page 15: LA 18 defense roster
